newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backed yld spreads continue to narrow.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backed yld spreads continue to narrow.

text.p: Light buying and selling took U.S. mortgage-backed securities on a bumpy ride to slightly lower levels, but yield spreads continued to narrow to Treasuries, traders said.
Current-coupon pass-throughs opened higher but pared gains to slight losses by late Wednesday afternoon, while comparable Treasuries were as much as 8/32 lower.
"The market has been interesting today, but I haven't heard any good reasons why," said one regional trader. "There was a little (buying) but nothing big," he added.

Market analysts said investors may have been overwhelmed by the $17.5 million supply of two-year notes. And government bonds may continue to selloff as the Treasury is expected to auction $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Thursday, they said.
Mortgage-backed traders cheered the narrowing of yield spreads over the past few days, and one attributed the recent trend to the lack of supply.
"(Investors) just assume there is no production right now and they have to be invested so they are buying mortgages," he said.
Nevertheless, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 3/32 at 99-27/32, yielding 105 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 3/32 loweras well, at 99-23/32 and 99-29/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 8/32 at 99-21/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
